source.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-layer Convolutional Neural Networks
source.authors: Yuan Cao; Zixiang Chen; Mikhail Belkin; Quanquan Gu

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops theoretical results about benign versus harmful overfitting in a two-layer CNN, but it does not test a double-descent curve along model size, epochs, or sample size, or any other listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper describes double-descent results from prior work in its related-work section. Its own theorems give training- and test-loss bounds under different signal-to-noise-ratio conditions; these do not establish a fall-rise-fall curve or a peak along any of the claim's axes. The theoretical loss results are recorded below as findings that fit no listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper proves benign vs harmful overfitting conditions for a two-layer CNN under an SNR condition. It gives no risk curve along model size, epochs or samples, and no peak at an interpolation threshold. Double descent appears only in related work. The theorems concern benign overfitting, a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also state the phase transition is with respect to sample size, signal strength, noise level and dimension. They say it shows benign overfitting can occur in neural network training beyond the NTK regime.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives a theoretical analysis of gradient descent on a specific two-layer CNN and synthetic signal-plus-noise data model, rather than testing a double-descent curve with an empirical sweep over model size, epochs, or sample size.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors' theoretical outcome depends on the signal-to-noise-ratio regime; their stated guarantees also require Condition 4.2 and other theorem-specific assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.3/4.4: an overfitted two-layer CNN (training loss ≤ ε) has test loss ≤ 6ε+exp(−n²) when n·SNR^q = Ω̃(1). It has Θ(1) test loss when n⁻¹·SNR⁻q = Ω̃(1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a two-layer ReLU^q CNN on signal-plus-noise patch data, a sharp phase transition between benign and harmful overfitting is set by n·SNR^q.

record.problems: The findings are theoretical and conditional on a particular data model, architecture, and restrictive assumptions; the paper does not empirically sweep the claim's axes or measure double-descent peaks.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep or peak; Condition 4.2 assumes d much larger than n and m (always overparameterized).
No test-loss trajectory over iterations showing fall-rise-fall; only existence of a good iterate within T.
n·SNR^q condition implies more samples favour benign overfitting, but there is no sample sweep near an interpolation threshold showing harm.
No capacity-risk curve across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting a peak location.
The paper analyses a feature-noise SNR, not label noise driving a peak; there are no multiple peaks and no regularization tuning.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are fine as theoretical bound rows with no linked versions. The paper is purely theoretical with no experiments. Belkin is a coauthor, but this paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or measurement of a peak near the training-set interpolation threshold.
No test-error curve over training epochs or time.
No sample-size sweep measuring whether more data raises test error near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity-versus-risk curve across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across axes.

The paper analyzes signal-to-noise-ratio conditions for benign versus harmful overfitting, but does not test whether label noise or variance drives a double-descent peak, multiple peaks, or the effect of optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters or test of whether that changes the curve's shape.
